thread.title: Stocks Bounce On Biggest Short-Squeeze Since Brexit, But Banks & Bullion Bruised

author: kring
title: Stocks Bounce On Biggest Short-Squeeze Since Brexit, But Banks & Bullion Bruised
text: May 4, 2018 Today's miss for payrolls, drop in unemployment, weaker wage growth, and drop in participation rate was proclaimed by Bob Pisani and his like as "goldilocks"... David Rosenberg disagreed:My grade for today’s payroll report is a big fat C-. Harsh, yes, given the apparent good news in the 3.9% u-rate, but this does not reflect job market strength as much as the symptom of an ever-depleted pool of labor (11-year low). Stocks - Week - Thanks - Squeeze - Brexit But for now, stocks ended the week unchanged thanks to the biggest short squeeze since Brexit to reassure everyone that...On the week, stocks mixed (Nasdaq up, Dow down); Dollar, Oil, and Bitcoin up; Gold down, bonds unch... Friday - Thursday - Momo - Reversal - Nasdaq Friday saw Thursday's momo reversal extend with Nasdaq and Small Caps squeezed into the green for the week and then S&P and The Dow pumped to green for the week after Fed's Williams comments that he's ok overshooting 2% inflation for a while... but by the close only Nasdaq and Small Caps held gains on the week...Futures show this was not related to payrolls - this was pure cash market short squeeze that began as Europe closed yesterday... Today - % - Stock - Day Today was a huge 3.3% "Most Shorted Stock" short-squeeze day...VIX flash-crashed to a 10-handle as payrolls printed... Time - March - Payrolls - Day and closed with a 14-handle for the first time since March 9th (payrolls day!)... and look what happened right before that low?!AAPL shares ripped to a new record high...
